recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Bio: Michelle Lundquist describes herself as a folk herbalist, gardener and homemaker with a passion for plants and their ability to heal. She has studied and actively worked with herbs since 2013, drawing most of her knowledge from hands on experience and mentors of the wise woman tradition, and a do it yourself spirit runs through her work as she encourages people to take their wellbeing into their own hands. She hosted more than eighty episodes of The Healing Home podcast as a kitchen witch, homemaker and folk herbalist, and now co-hosts Symbolic Studies with her husband Mario Garza.
recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Name: Michelle Lundquist

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Dandelion, Burdock and the Liver Fire", "body": "Kyle chose dandelion as the first Sagittarius herb, saying its abundance, its growth in all directions and its mutable nature matched Jupiter signatures. He described dandelion root as a liver herb for the hot, overworked, mutable fire type, and tied the liver to anger that a single-minded archer might hold back. Kyle said burdock worked in similar ways, calling it a blood purifier in Appalachian folk medicine, and joked that its burrs stick to the hips and thighs, the Sagittarian parts of the body. He framed both as aids to nutrition, not weight loss."}, {"title": "Bear Medicine and the Burry Man", "body": "Kyle presented burdock and osha as bear medicine, explaining that the bear wakes from winter looking for oily roots. He said the bear, in Native American medicine, is linked with the polestar and dreams, and described going into the depths of the psyche to come out the other side. Kyle said he used osha in a lung tonic that Chance sometimes received. He also shared the Burry Man festival of South Queensferry in Scotland, where a person covered in burrs is walked around for nine hours, and the group traded readings of its symbolism."}, {"title": "Temperance Card and Sagittarius Wordplay", "body": "The show opened with the Temperance card, which Kyle used as a loom for symbolism, calling Sagittarius the tarrying sage. Gabe noted that the sign has three minor decans, Lyra, the Altar and Draco, and linked the card's cauldron to the Altar. Chance described his reading that the Sumerian word sag means head, beginning or first, and tied it to sage and wisdom. Mario brought the world axis and the idea that stems of plants echo it. Chance also shared biofield views on the hips, as his own findings."}, {"title": "Clove, Frankincense, Bilberry and Sage", "body": "Kyle presented clove as a warming spice road herb that fit the travel theme of Sagittarius, and said its nail shape invited symbolism. Others in the group tied nails to binding, and the name syzygy came up. Kyle framed frankincense as resin from a wounded tree, sacred across many cultures, and linked it to the gifts of the Magi, which prompted wordplay and trinity weaves among the group. He said bilberry suited the sign through its eye signature and recounted a World War I pilot story. He closed the herb slides with clary sage for clarity and vision, and described making sage honey."}, {"title": "Reishi and the Return of Shen", "body": "Michelle brought reishi as a clear example of Jupiter expansion, pointing to its growth rings and calling it an adaptogen, an herb she said helps the body adapt and balance. Another speaker explained the Chinese idea of shen, the spirit housed in the heart, said reishi was used to gather the spirit back after prolonged fear, and mentioned that it is called the emperor's mushroom. Others in the group tied the name to ten, the Aeon card and the torus, and one guest described mushrooms as the DNA of the forest."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: It's time to take a look at Sagittarius signatures, with our resident herbalists, Kyle Denton of Tippecanoe Herbs and Ms. Lundquist of Michelle's Healing Home. Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies will be in the mix too, adding his observations about the season of the far-sighted archer.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I think the world tree symbolism, by extension, can kind of be applied to a lot of other plants, seeing how a lot of flowers and trees and herbs, they have that main shoot, that main stem that goes upward, reminds me very much of the world axis, the world pole.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "One of my first teachers gave me a really good piece of advice, and that was, learn one herb very well in and out throughout the week. So you make tea with it, you study it, you put it under your pillow, you sleep, you meditate with it, all these things. And by the end of the year, you have a really strong repertory of 52 herbs.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Burdock invented hairy dogs in blue jeans, because the reason it gets around is by sticking to your hips and thighs when you're walking through the woods. So going into the depths of winter, going into the depths of your own psyche in order to come out to the other side or to come out through the center.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "It feels so great to be the type of herbalist that I want to be, which is very nerdy and just talk about the strange things about nature. I feel like there's not a lot of room for that in the dogmatic practice of anything right now, and including an art so lovely as herbalism.", "author": "Kyle Denton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/3bfe296c-3dcd-4af6-bc2e-26466a87ec04/KYLE-DENTON.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "We cover every sign in the herbs and the doctrine of signatures, AKA the shapes, patterns, geometries, smells, correlations and syncretism of these beautiful herbs, plants, mushrooms, all of their many, many, I won't even wanna say qualities, but virtues, as Kyle likes to say.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I looked deeper into the word sag, S-A-G, which is of course like the word sage. It can also mean beginning or first. So sag as a sage is wisdom.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I feel like all the time I'm just like, how did I get this job?
